subject: Money
title: The Great Depression Bank Panic
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Great Depression Bank Panic.

hook.text: Between 1929 and 1933, 9,000 US banks failed. One-third of all banks vanished in four years.

buildup.text: The Fed kept money tight when it should have eased. Banks couldn't get cash. Depositors couldn't get savings.

discovery.text: Bank failures destroyed savings, which killed spending, which killed businesses, which caused more bank failures.

twist.text: FDR declared a bank holiday in 1933—closing every bank for four days. When they reopened, panic had cooled.

climax.text: The Depression taught a brutal lesson: letting banks fail freely destroys the real economy, not just Wall Street.

punchline.text: Let the banks fall. Watch everything follow.

quiz.question: How many US banks failed during the Great Depression?
